title: Computer vision
reading: The slide defines computer vision as the setting where the data consist of images, videos, or signals captured by 3D sensors. A montage of application photographs surrounds the single bullet, illustrating the breadth of domains in which such visual data arise.

visuals.description: Seven-image montage: industrial machine-vision cameras on a rail, a smartphone photographing a flower, a self-driving car, a camera-equipped drone over farmland, a clinician reviewing medical brain scans on multiple monitors, people playing Kinect Sports in front of a TV, and a VR/AR headset.
visuals.assertion: Computer vision underpins applications across industrial inspection, mobile photography, autonomous driving, aerial imaging, medical imaging, gesture-based gaming, and virtual/augmented reality.

concepts.name: Computer vision
concepts.why_it_matters: Frames the subfield handled when data are visual rather than tabular or textual.

concepts.name: 3D sensors
